provenance.dpm_state: high-forced (power_dpm_force_performance_level=high; warm DPM-warmup protocol per docs/methodology/perf-benchmarking.md)
provenance._note: WITHHELD (issue #490): prior mem_latency_ns=148.035 ns was CACHE-DEFLATED — the fixed 128 MiB pointer-chase buffer fit ENTIRELY inside this part's 128 MiB Infinity Cache (L2 4 + IC 128 = 132 MiB). Re-measure under the per-arch >=4x(L2+IC)=528 MiB buffer + chip_profile::check_residency guard before restoring a value. RX 6950 XT / gfx1030 (RDNA2), hipx zoo card, WARM force-high mclk sweep, 2026-07-02. Static fields (vgprs_per_simd=1024, max_waves_per_simd=20, lds_bytes_per_cu=65536, wavefront_size=32) are read directly from the single source of truth profiler.rs::arch_spec('gfx1030'|...'gfx1036' RDNA2 arm) + ArchCaps::is_wave32() — not hand-recalled. cu_count=80 is from rocminfo/KFD topology on the live card (the 6950 XT is the full Navi 21 die at 80 CU; profiler.rs's fallback const 'gfx1030'=>60 is the smaller RX 6800 SKU and correctly does NOT apply here — this row is a different SKU with its own committed profile per the module docs' per-device-row rule). vram_mb=16384 (16GB RX 6950 XT). mem_latency_ns=148.035 is MEASURED WARM via pointer_chase_latency at power_dpm_force_performance_level=high. peak_bw_gbps=498.1 is the DRAM-bound large-buffer PLATEAU from the peak_bw_probe multi-tier sweep (chip_profile::detect_bw_tiers). cache_bw_gbps=1586.5 / effective_cache_mib=64.0: RDNA2's 128MB Infinity Cache (profiler.rs::arch_spec infinity_cache_mb=128.0 for this family) DOES show a real cache tier in the swept curve — the cache-resident row's peak BW (1586.5 GB/s) clears the DRAM plateau (498.1 GB/s) by >3x, so detect_bw_tiers reports it as a genuine tier (per the 'cache peak must exceed DRAM plateau' guard added 2026-07-02, this is the positive case — contrast with gfx1010's null tier, which fails that guard). effective_cache_mib=64.0 is the largest swept buffer size that stayed cache-resident before the curve dropped to the DRAM plateau — smaller than the chip's full 128MB Infinity Cache because this probe's swept sizes bracket transitions at fixed sample points, not the die's exact capacity; treat this as the empirical 'still cache-resident' boundary the probe observed, not a spec claim.
